styleGuard.era: Pre-industrial and pre-electric throughout. Roads are rutted dirt tracks of bare earth and cart ruts. Every vehicle is a wooden ox-drawn cart or a handcart. Every structure is built from timber, canvas, thatch, daub, fired brick and dressed stone, lit by daylight and open flame.
styleGuard._note: CORRECTED 2026-08-08 (F-039). This block used to be `negative: ["no cars", "no trucks", "no modern vehicles", "no power lines", "no paved roads", "no contemporary architecture", "no modern city skyline"]`, and buildEnvPositive() appended that list verbatim into the POSITIVE prompt. The previous note claimed the list "REDUCES but does not ELIMINATE" modern contamination. THAT CLAIM IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE INHERITED: the list did not reduce contamination, it CAUSED it. A diffusion text encoder attends to tokens and has no operator for negation, so every one of those seven phrases delivered its own subject -- cars, trucks, power lines, paved roads, modern city skyline -- straight into the conditioning. EVIDENCE. (1) docs/worldbuilding/ABP-controlnet-replication.md, 16 cells: lattice pylons in 5 of 16, SUV-like vehicles and hazy modern skylines in 3 more, explicitly "despite 'no modern vehicles'/'no modern city skyline' already being in this list" -- read correctly, that is the list working exactly as a token list works. (2) The same doc records rubble on Cindervast (A1-ART-07) in 4 of 4 cells on a brief that asked for clean stonework -- and that brief's own prose said "there is no rubble". (3) Millcross re-run 2026-08-08 at ControlNet strength 0.00/0.30/0.45/0.60: pylons and painted road markings in EVERY cell, including with the control signal fully OFF, which rules the control image out as the source. A positive-only rewrite of the same subject came back clean -- river, ford, cart queue, a real water-wheel, no pylons, no markings, no vehicles. THE FIX is `era`: one shared positive assertion of what IS present, appended to every environment positive prompt in the slot the negative list used to occupy. Its wording is the measured-good prompt's era paragraph with ONE deliberate deviation: the measured version ended "The horizon is open farmland and low hills", which is true of Millcross and false of the tidal flat (A1-ART-06) and the upland rock shoulder (A1-ART-07), so the horizon stays brief-owned; and the material list is widened with fired brick and dressed stone for the brick/stone subjects. That deviation is NOT yet re-measured on a GPU. `forbiddenTokens` is the same modern-contamination vocabulary kept as DATA rather than as prompt text: generate/prompt-lint.mjs (R2) throws if any of these words appears in a composed positive prompt, so the old list can never be re-appended by accident. It deliberately omits 'cart', 'road' and 'pole', which are legitimate pre-industrial content, and 'vehicle', which `era` itself uses. SUPERSEDED HISTORY (kept because the replication cells were generated under it): "Measured directly from this recipe's first real generation — A1-ART-02 'Millcross' (a pre-industrial crossing town) rendered as a photorealistic MODERN settlement: white pickup trucks, an SUV, corrugated-metal roofing, a contemporary city skyline on the horizon. The ABP's own recorded workflow carried a bare prompt (it was measuring ControlNet strength, not style) and neither the brief prose nor the shared style-laws.json ruled out modern contamination — schnell defaults toward a photoreal modern read once style words are absent. REPLICATED 2026-08-03 (docs/worldbuilding/ABP-controlnet-replication.md) across the other three L1 briefs, two seeds, strengths 0.30/0.40: this list REDUCES but does not ELIMINATE modern contamination — 1 of 16 cells still showed SUV-like vehicles plus wooden utility poles/wires (Millcross, seed 741852), and 2 of 16 showed a hazy modern city skyline in the background (Cindervast, both seeds, strength 0.30) despite 'no modern vehicles'/'no modern city skyline' already being in this list. Two artifact classes this list does NOT target at all and should: a recurring electricity-transmission LATTICE-PYLON silhouette (5 of 16 cells, 3 of 4 subjects, clustered on seed 12345) and visibly cracked/rubbled walls on subjects whose brief explicitly calls for clean stonework (Cindervast, 4 of 4 cells)."

environment._note: Measured in docs/worldbuilding/ABP-controlnet-rescue.md (Gildmark, Norhollow) and REPLICATED 2026-08-03 in docs/worldbuilding/ABP-controlnet-replication.md across the four remaining L1 towns (Millcross, Embervale, Rooktide, Cindervast), two seeds (12345, 741852), both ends of the strength window (0.30, 0.40) — 16/16 generations completed, 0 OOMs. strength 0.30 is NOT a typo: the usable window is 0.30-0.40 and the conventional 0.8-1.0 collapses schnell into flat vector art (-88% detail). Steps and strength interact — 8 steps at strength >= 0.50 produced a cutout halo. Do not reach for end_percent to fix flatness; reach for lower strength. THE STRENGTH/PAINT-QUALITY CLAIM HOLDS: all 16 replication cells stayed painted, 0 flat-vector collapses, across four new subjects — that part of the recipe is now evidenced on six subjects; two seeds on four of them, not two subjects, one seed. THE PROFILE AS A WHOLE DOES NOT YET CLEAR AN UNATTENDED-BATCH BAR, but not because of Embervale: rendering and viewing Embervale's own depth control map directly (docs/worldbuilding/ABP-controlnet-replication.md, re-attributed section) shows it is itself a symmetric, centred, stepped pyramid, and the 4/4 generations matched that shape faithfully. This is CONFIRMED as a block-in composition-authoring defect, not a recipe or strength defect, and is now read as evidence of HIGH depth-adherence, not an open question — see the ABP's new Authoring-law section (symmetric, centred stacks of steps render as one monument; terraced settlements need asymmetric, off-centre, broken masses). What still blocks unattended-batch use is a separate, unrelated axis: content control (hallucinated text/emblems, modern contamination, the rubble/wall-condition miss on Cindervast) remains unsuppressed in nearly a third of cells. See styleGuard._note above for what the replication found about modern-contamination and lattice-pylon recurrence. Still unswept: steps=16 on any subject, and strengths 0.40-0.60 on the four newly-tested subjects (only 0.30/0.40 were run). Checkpoint filename flux1-schnell-fp8.safetensors and ControlNet filename flux-controlnet-union-pro-2.0.safetensors were both VERIFIED to exist on the live ComfyUI server (v0.24.1) on 2026-08-02 via GET /object_info/CheckpointLoaderSimple and GET /object_info/ControlNetLoader respectively — this confirms the filenames are installed, and the 2026-08-03 replication confirms 16/16 real generations against them completed without error.
